title: Apple has a new way to prove your iPhone photos aren’t AI slop
slides: Can Apple prove your iPhone photos aren't AI fakes?
The company just patented a cryptographic watermarking system.
But it works by embedding your personal ID in every shot.
Your photos will now carry an invisible digital signature.
Check your camera settings—this may already be opt-in.
thread_text:
1. Apple's Watermark Plan

A new patent embeds your personal ID into every iPhone photo via cryptographic watermarking.

2. Invisible Signature

Each shot gets a hidden digital signature that can prove it's not AI-generated.

3. How It Works

The system ties your identity to the image, raising privacy concerns if misused.

4. Opt-In Already?

Check your camera settings—this feature may already be enabled by default.

5. Your Next Move

Open your camera app and look for 'Provenance' or 'Watermark' options. Turn it off if you don't want your ID embedded.

instagram.caption:
Every iPhone photo may soon carry a hidden digital signature tied to your personal ID.

Apple patented a cryptographic watermarking system that embeds your identity into each shot.

The goal: prove a photo isn't AI-generated by linking it to a real device and a real person.

But that same signature stays invisible inside the file, even when you share it. 🔐

If you post photos for work, your name could travel with every image you upload. 📸

Open your camera app, look for "Provenance" or "Watermark" settings, and decide if you want it on. 🔍

Would you trade privacy for proof your photos are real? 🤔
